subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and hooks?
rationale: The feature is a security-relevant product guarantee, and current source shows multiple execution surfaces that a narrow process-global adapter flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

options.title: Fold into broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Leave scoped command-level dry-runs only if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misunderstand as a full sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/security-contract shaped, and this handle has substantial history in the tool adapter and hook execution path.
